b: Rare systemic disease caused by bacillus Tropheryma whipplei
Affects small intestine, CNS, joints, heart
Pathogenesis: bacteria engulfed by macrophages → accumulation in lamina propria
Small intestine: lamina propria distended by foamy macrophages containing PAS-positive material (bacterial remnants)
Macrophages impair lymphatic drainage and villous function

qs.q: Whipple disease is a chronic systemic infection caused by which type of organism?
qs.e: Whipple disease is caused by Tropheryma whipplei, which is an intracellular gram-positive bacterium. The organism infiltrates the small intestinal lamina propria and mesenteric lymph nodes.

qs.q: Which histological staining technique is most specific for identifying the causal agent of Whipple disease in small bowel biopsies?
qs.e: Numerous periodic acid-Schiff (PAS)-positive granular particles representing lysosomes filled with T. whipplei are very specific for Whipple disease. Routine H&E typically shows characteristic foamy macrophages.

qs.q: What is the initial phase of antibiotic therapy designed to cross the blood-brain barrier for treating Whipple disease?
o: Vancomycin and metronidazole for six weeks.
Ceftriaxone IV or Penicillin G plus streptomycin.
qs.e: Initial treatment involves 2 weeks of antibiotics that cross the blood-brain barrier, such as IV ceftriaxone or penicillin G plus streptomycin, followed by long-term oral therapy. TMP-SMX is used for the maintenance phase rather than the initial induction.

qs.q: Why do patients with Whipple disease frequently present with fatty diarrhea?
o: Macrophage infiltration obstructing mesenteric lymph nodes.
Direct destruction of jejunal brush‑border enzymes.
Rapid transit due to autonomic neuropathy.
qs.e: Malabsorption of fat in Whipple disease is caused by bacterial and macrophage-predominant inflammatory cell infiltration of the small intestinal mucosa and obstruction of mesenteric lymph nodes. Pancreatic enzyme secretion is typically normal.

qs.q: A 50-year-old man is diagnosed with Whipple disease following duodenal biopsy. Which extraintestinal finding is most frequently documented years before the onset of prominent gastrointestinal complaints?
qs.e: Intermittent migratory seronegative oligoarthritis or polyarthralgias frequently precede diarrhea and weight loss by years in Whipple disease. Uveitis and erythema nodosum are significantly less common initial presentations.

qs.q: A 55-year-old man with weight loss, abdominal pain, diarrhea, and arthropathy; small bowel biopsy shows PAS-positive inclusions in the bowel wall. Which test could confirm Whipple disease, caused by Tropheryma whipplei?
o: Polymerase chain reaction amplification and sequencing
qs.e: *T. whipplei* is very difficult to culture on standard media, so molecular methods (PCR/sequencing) are the standard confirmatory diagnostic approach.
